function: Joint BS beamforming and RIS phase-shift design maximizing energy efficiency under rate and power constraints; the GNN outputs beamformers and RIS phases from channels (p. 6-7)
system: Downlink MISO: BS with M=4 antennas, reflecting RIS with N=64 elements, T=3 single-antenna UEs; cell-free extension; 1 MHz bandwidth, carrier frequency not stated (p. 3, 9, 10, 13)
method: Heterogeneous graph neural network (embedding, K=3 message-passing layers, mapping), vertex- and edge-initialized variants; unsupervised offline training with Dinkelbach or negative-EE loss (p. 6-8)
data_channel: Own simulator: log-distance path loss with CN(0,1) small-scale fading, random UE positions; 11,000 samples, 10,000 for training and 1,000 for testing (p. 8, 10)
test_conditions: Train and test with T=3 UEs, N=64 (p. 9); mismatched user counts T=3-9 (Table IV, p. 12); pre-trained with 3 RISs, tested with other counts (p. 13)
baselines: Classical: AO (SCA, SDR), random phase, no RIS; learned: fully connected DNN [29] with the same unsupervised loss (p. 9)
metrics: Energy efficiency, sum-rate, target ratio (share of test samples meeting the rate constraint), training and inference time (p. 9-12)
complexity: Forward complexity O(K T^2 E) (p. 9); Table III (p. 12): VIGNN inference 1.02 s CPU, 0.27 s GPU, training 1.82e3 s for T=3
q1_support: p. 9: "the main simulation parameters are listed in Table I"; Table I (p. 10) gives log-distance path loss and CN(0,1) small-scale fading, a custom simulator. No 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "Table IV presents the generalization capability of the VIGNN model under varying numbers of training and testing UEs" (trained on T = 3, tested on T = 9); p. 13: "the model is pre-trained with LRIS = 3 and then tested with varying numbers of RISs".
q3_support: p. 9: "DNN: A fully-connected deep neural network [29]", listed with the AO, Random Phase and No RIS baselines; p. 12: "the proposed GNN-based framework consistently outperforms all baselines across the entire transmit power range" (EE, Fig. 9).
q4_support: p. 9: "the total computational complexity of the forward process is" given as an order in K, T and E for VIGNN and EIGNN; p. 12: Table III reports training and inference times in seconds on CPU and GPU.
q5_support: p. 8: "The total generated dataset consists of 11 000 samples" from the authors' own simulator; no code or data link and no public dataset or measurement; only the PyG, PyTorch and Gurobi libraries are cited.
notes: Published version, IEEE TWC 2026, pp. 664-680. Area 3: joint BS beamformer and RIS phase design for energy efficiency.
